- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for 1–3 week horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–25% for 1–3 week horizons.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00), producing exaggerated 30d peaks; apply smoothing filter to dampen 3–5 day spikes.
- Forecasts show mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 2.5x historical mean, reduce by 20–40% for 1–2 week horizons.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 3x historical max in 3–5 days, model is likely overfitting; apply downward correction based on sentiment decay (e.g., if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast by 10–20%).
- Model underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) — increase forecast by 5–15% for 1–3 week horizons.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive positive values, model tends to overforecast; apply 10–20% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
